clue.text: Trouble in orchards, unusually brief and inconsequential

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the following word are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: something inconsequential is light, of little weight or importance

explanation.surface: A complaint about orchard troubles being dismissed as brief and trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief and inconsequential' reads as a description of the trouble, but 'unusually' is the anagram signal on 'brief'.
explanation.definitionFit: This bacterial disease scorches pear and apple trees, a serious problem for fruit growers.

clue.text: Piece of documentary film, reduced — and shortened

definitions.text: Piece of documentary film, reduced — and shortened

parts.words: Piece of documentary film, reduced — and shortened
parts.note: describes a sheet of film holding documents at reduced size, whose name is itself a clipped form of a longer word

explanation.surface: A clip from a documentary cut down for broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'documentary film' suggests television; it is film carrying documents in miniature, and the word itself is shortened from microfiche.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat sheet of microfilm stores pages of print at very small size.

clue.text: Proof against train-sets being damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A toy railway that survives rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being damaged' rearranges TRAIN-SETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impervious to something means withstanding it, as in waterproof.

clue.text: Boating, radioed for repair? Breaking down, naturally

indicators.note: sent for repair suggests the letters are taken apart and reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A boat whose radio has broken and needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for repair?' rearranges BOATING and RADIOED together.
explanation.definitionFit: Decomposition by bacteria and other living organisms is a natural process of decay.

clue.text: Royal visitor from Spain, intrigued by freak tree in nursery?

definitions.text: Royal visitor from Spain, intrigued by freak tree in nursery?

parts.words: Royal visitor from Spain, intrigued by freak tree in nursery?
parts.note: recalls the nursery rhyme 'I had a little nut tree', where the King of Spain's daughter came to visit for the sake of the tree

explanation.surface: A Spanish royal touring a children's garden, fascinated by an odd tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, the nut tree bears a silver nutmeg and a golden pear and draws the King of Spain's daughter; 'freak' is a nut, an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter of the Spanish king is given this title.

clue.text: Bone's vibration sure to be troublesome

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a hum is a low vibrating sound

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the letters are disturbed and put out of order

explanation.surface: A bone that hums and is sure to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone's' looks possessive, but the 's means 'is'; 'to be troublesome' is the anagram signal on 'sure'.
explanation.definitionFit: The long bone of the upper arm, running from shoulder to elbow.

clue.text: Blow this hairstyle!

definitions.meaning: in American usage ... are a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a hairdo gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud knock is a sudden blow, and the US word for a straight-cut fringe is the same word.

clue.text: A time to show up in amphitheatre

indicators.note: in a down clue, showing up means rising, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a time is an era, so A TIME gives AN ERA

explanation.surface: A good moment to appear at the Colosseum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to show up' turns AN ERA upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman amphitheatre had a central sanded area where contests took place.

clue.text: Gordon-led riot a bloomer

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters run riot into another order

explanation.surface: A riot led by a man named Gordon turned out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' rearranges GORDON-LED. The Gordon Riots of 1780 colour the surface; 'bloomer' is a mistake on the surface but a flower here.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall plant has yellow flower spikes, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: How explicit was A. Brontë under cover?

definitions.meaning: the phrase describes something perfectly plain and easy to understand
Anne Brontë published under the pen name Acton Bell, so in disguise she was as a Bell

explanation.surface: Asking how clearly Anne Brontë wrote when using a pseudonym.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontë sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crystal clear is perfectly explicit, as unmistakable as a ringing chime.

clue.text: Abandoned cricket side on pitch

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: to pitch is to throw, or cast
the off side is one half of a cricket field, opposite the leg side

explanation.surface: A cricket team walking off and leaving its pitch behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The OFF side in cricket is the half of the field the batter faces, the other half being the leg or on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something discarded or rejected, like old clothes, has been thrown away and abandoned.

clue.text: Improper distribution to players at start

definitions.text: Improper distribution to players at start

indicators.note: at start places the first piece at the beginning, before the other

parts.note: the prefix mis- means wrongly or improperly
a deal is the handing out of cards to the players

explanation.surface: Unfair sharing out among sportsmen at the start of a season.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer too: a faulty deal happens at the very start of a card game. 'players' suggests sport or theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A faulty dealing of cards, which must then be redone before play can begin.

clue.text: Oriental poet's always comprehending a grave

indicators.note: comprehending means taking in or including, so the poet's word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
a grave expression is a stern one

explanation.surface: A poem about an Oriental who always understands a solemn tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective; 'comprehending' puts A plus that adjective inside the poet's contraction of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the East, such as Asia, is an Oriental in the older sense.

clue.text: The French hail and farewell

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
ave is the Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: French greetings at arrival and departure.
explanation.walkthrough: AVE, as in 'Ave Maria', is Latin for hail.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave in the sense of formal permission to depart, as in taking one's leave, is a farewell.

clue.text: Waylay in a section of flight

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a lay is a song or ballad, as is an air

explanation.surface: Ambushing someone partway through a plane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waylay' reads as one word meaning ambush, but it splits into WAY and LAY. A flight here is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: One step is a single part of a staircase, which is called a flight.

clue.text: No works of Landseer, might one presume?

definitions.text: No works of Landseer, might one presume?

parts.words: No works of Landseer, might one presume?
parts.note: splits the painter's name into land and seer, so his paintings would not be of the ocean

explanation.surface: An art critic doubting that Landseer painted certain pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter of animals; his name read as LAND-SEER suggests he would only paint the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings of the ocean are marine pictures, the opposite of landscapes.

clue.text: He avoids the bishop in a Barset novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A character in one of Trollope's Barsetshire novels who keeps away from the bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges IN A BARSET. Bishop is also a mulled port drink, which a teetotaller avoids; Trollope's Barset novels are full of clergy, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller refuses alcohol, including bishop, a hot spiced wine.

clue.text: Naturalness of average resort of Italy

parts.note: the norm is the average or standard

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The natural charm of a typical Italian holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but means re-sort: ITALY becomes ALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being usual and unforced is a natural condition.

clue.text: Countering ill-feeling in opponent of union presentation

parts.note: an anti is someone who is against something
dotal means relating to a dowry, a gift presented on marriage

explanation.surface: Fighting resentment by staging a show for a trade union opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks industrial but is marriage: DOTAL describes a dowry.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy works against poison or illness, so the adjective means counteracting sickness.

clue.text: Earth's surface covers valuable raw material

parts.note: tops are lids or covers
crude oil is a valuable raw material

explanation.surface: The Earth's crust hides precious resources such as petroleum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' looks like the verb linking the parts, but it is TOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper layer of soil is the ground's surface, where plants grow.

clue.text: Guard's concern

definitions.meaning: as in that's your ..., meaning your own affair

explanation.surface: A sentry's worries.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchman keeps guard, and the British idiom 'your lookout' means your own business or concern.

clue.text: Bitter's free, going by the bill

indicators.note: going by means passing alongside, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A pub drinker delighted the beer is free, judging by the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' reads as the British beer, but the definition is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, pungent taste or smell is sharp and bitter.

clue.text: Have one's eye on bloke Times leader's on

parts.note: cove is old slang for a man or bloke

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the word Times

explanation.surface: Desiring a man whose newspaper editorial is published.
explanation.walkthrough: A leader is also a newspaper editorial, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: To desire something belonging to another is to want it eagerly.

clue.text: Clergyman detained by civic architect

indicators.note: detained by means held inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A priest held captive by a city's architect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detained by' holds the run inside CIVIC ARCHITECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England holds this title.

clue.text: Suitable for listener, opening broadcast

indicators.note: said for a listener, the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: proper means suitable or fitting
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast deemed suitable for listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the final R of the word for suitable is not sounded. 'opening' looks like the definition next to 'broadcast', but it supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread ideas or plants widely is to disseminate them, as a broadcast does.

clue.text: Large unorthodox music-maker

indicators.note: unorthodox means unconventional, so the letters stray from their usual order

explanation.surface: An eccentric, large musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges LARGE. Edward Elgar was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar, composer of the Enigma Variations, made music for a living.

clue.text: In the wind, it goes higher than the rest

definitions.text: In the wind, it goes higher than the rest

parts.words: In the wind, it goes higher than the rest
parts.note: describes the small flute that plays the highest notes of the woodwind section

explanation.surface: Something blown high above the others by a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' suggests weather; it is the woodwind section of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: This little flute sounds an octave above the ordinary flute, the top voice of the woodwinds.

clue.text: Chance for expanding

explanation.surface: An opportunity to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourable opportunity is a chance, and unfolding something is making it spread wider.

clue.text: Eastern garment I put on 14, oddly

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another comes after it
oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters of the answer the cross-reference names

parts.note: the cross-reference points to 14 across, a section of flight

explanation.surface: A woman wearing an Eastern robe over something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of STAIR (14 across), giving SAR, and I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrapped length of cloth worn by Indian women is a traditional Eastern dress.

clue.text: Actor slow to come in? His job's on the line

indicators.note: to come in means to enter, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a player is an actor
late can mean slow or behind time

explanation.surface: A tardy actor missing his cue, his career at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the line' suggests a job at risk; it is a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: This worker lays and maintains railway track, so the work is literally on the rails.
